paragraphs: Art. 1. (1) The territory of the Republic of Bulgaria is a national asset. Its development guarantees sustainable development and favourable conditions for living, work and recreation of the population.

(2) This act regulates the public relations connected with spatial development, investment design and construction in the Republic of Bulgaria, and sets the restrictions on ownership for spatial development purposes.

Art. 7. (1) According to their basic purpose, set by the concepts and schemes for spatial development and the general development plans, the territories in the country are: urbanised territories (settlements, settlement formations and industrial parks outside the boundaries of the settlements and settlement formations), agricultural territories, forest territories, protected territories, damaged territories for recovery, territories covered by water and water objects, and territories of transport.
(2) Territories with an agricultural, forest or urbanised purpose may at the same time have the purpose of protected territories set by law.
Art. 8. The specific purpose of the land plots is set by the detailed development plan and may be:

1. in urbanised territories or in separate land plots outside them: for housing, public services, production, storage, resort, villa, sports and entertainment functions, for green areas and green links between them and the territories for nature protection, for decorative water systems (cascades, navigable canals and others), for traffic and transport, including cycle lanes and access for persons with disabilities, for technical infrastructure, for special objects and others;
2. in agricultural territories: for arable land (fields, orchards and vegetable gardens, vineyards, meadows and others) and non-arable land (pastures, slopes, gullies, ravines and others);
3. in forest territories: for forests (production, protective, recreational forests and others) and forest land (glades, land covered by shrubs, rocks and others);

4. in protected territories: for nature protection (nature reserves, national parks, natural landmarks, managed reserves, nature parks, protected sites, beaches, dunes, water sources with their sanitary protection zones, water areas, wetlands, protected coastal strips) and for the protection of the cultural and historical heritage (archaeological reserves, separate blocks or plots in settlements of cultural, historical, ethnographic or architectural importance);
5. in damaged territories: for recovery and reclamation of quarries, mines, dumps, tailings ponds, waste landfills, landslides, rockfalls and others;
6. in territories covered by water and water objects: for the internal sea waters and the territorial sea, the Bulgarian section of the Danube, the rivers, the lakes and the dams;
7. in territories of transport: for the national and local roads, the railway infrastructure, the ports and the airports.
Art. 12. (1) Building within the meaning of this act is the placing and construction of buildings, structures, networks and facilities in land plots.
(2) Building is allowed only if an effective detailed development plan provides for it, and after a change of the purpose of the land when a special law requires it.

(3) Without a change of purpose, objects whose functions suit the purpose of the plots under Art. 8, items 2, 3 and 4 may be built in those plots, in compliance with the regulations in force and on the basis of a detailed development plan or a design permit issued by the chief architect of the municipality.
Art. 14. (1) Detailed development plans regulate streets, as well as blocks and land plots for building and for other needs without building.
(2) Streets and blocks are regulated with street regulation lines.
(3) Land plots are regulated with:
1. street regulation lines, which set the boundary with the adjoining street (the frontage of the plot);
2. internal regulation lines, which set the boundaries with the neighbouring plots (at the sides and at the back of the plot), under the conditions of Art. 16 or 17.
(4) Regulated land plots must have frontage (an exit) to a street, to a road or, by exception, to an alley in a park.

(5) In land plots regulated by a detailed development plan, the regulation lines under para. 3 become the boundaries of the plots when the detailed development plan is implemented as to the regulation.

Art. 15. (1) A detailed development plan under Art. 16 or 17 regulates only land plots that were not regulated by a previous detailed development plan. Land plots regulated once are not subject to later regulation, except in the cases provided for in this act.
(2) A later detailed development plan may regulate only streets and blocks, without changing the boundaries between the land plots.

(3) The boundaries of regulated land plots may be changed by a regulation plan only with the consent of their owners, expressed by an application and a preliminary contract for the transfer of ownership with notarially certified signatures.
(4) When a regulation plan changes the boundaries of regulated land plots that are state property, the contract under para. 3 is concluded at market prices by the regional governor in written form.

(5) When a regulation plan changes the boundaries of regulated land plots that are municipal property, the contract under para. 3 is concluded at market prices by the mayor of the municipality in written form.
(6) The act approving the regulation plan that changes the boundaries between regulated land plots under para. 3 enters into force when issued and is communicated to the applicants.
(7) Building in regulated land plots whose boundaries are changed by the regulation plan under para. 3 is permitted after the final contract under para. 3, 4 or 5 is presented.
(8) Building in such plots is not permitted when, as a result of the change of the regulation plan, the building plan for these plots contradicts the development rules and norms in force.

(9) A change of a regulation plan under para. 3 is refused by an order of the mayor when the draft would create a position of existing buildings or permitted constructions that the law does not allow.

(10) A change of a regulation plan under para. 3 is refused by an order of the mayor when the draft would create regulated land plots with a frontage and an area below the minimum that the law sets for the character and manner of building of these plots.

(11) Copies of the effective changes of detailed development plans under para. 3 are sent by the municipality to the Geodesy, Cartography and Cadastre Agency of its own motion after the final contract under para. 3, 4 or 5 is presented.

Art. 16. (1) A detailed development plan for territories with unregulated land plots, and for territories where a first regulation under a previous plan was not implemented, sets the areas needed for the green system and for the social and technical infrastructure in public ownership. To carry this out, when the plan enters into force the owners of real estate transfer to the municipality a percentage of the area of their properties set by the plan, but not more than 25 per cent.
(2) The detailed development plan under para. 1 is prepared on the basis of a cadastral map approved under the Cadastre and Property Register Act.
(3) The frontage and the area of the newly formed regulated plots, their specific purpose, and the character and manner of their building are set by the detailed development plan itself.

(4) In the cases under para. 1, the municipality gives every owner of real estate an equivalent regulated plot (plots), taking into account the location of the properties in the area, but not their exact cadastral boundaries. When the property falls into different development zones, the new regulated plot is given in the zone where most of the property was. The regulated plots have a market value not lower than the market value of the properties before their regulation, which is proved by a decision of the commission under Art. 210. The decision of the commission is communicated to the persons concerned together with the draft plan and may be appealed in the proceedings against the act approving the plan under para. 1.
(5) With the plan under para. 1:
1. land plots that do not meet the minimum frontage and area of their development zone may be joined into one or more new regulated plots, if they belong to the same persons;
2. at the request of the owners, land plots owned by the same persons may be joined into one new regulated plot, and one land plot may be divided into two or more new regulated plots;

3. a co-owned regulated plot may be formed from two or more land plots of different persons, on the basis of a joint application of the owners with notarially certified signatures that sets the ideal parts of the co-owners, which are stated in the order under para. 6.

(6) The owners of land plots under paras. 4 and 5 acquire ownership of the regulated plots newly formed by the plan, and the municipality acquires ownership of the parts given up under para. 1, from the date on which the plan enters into force. For each regulated plot, the mayor or a person authorised by the mayor issues an order with an exact identification of the property. The orders are sent to the registry office, and a copy of the effective plan under para. 1 to the Geodesy, Cartography and Cadastre Agency, for entry in the property register and in the cadastre of their own motion.
(7) The mortgages on the land plots before their regulation pass in full to the newly created regulated plots. The municipality acquires the parts given up free of real encumbrances.

Art. 17. (1) Outside the cases under Art. 16, a detailed development plan for a settlement or a part of it regulates land plots not regulated so far, and their internal regulation lines follow the property boundaries.
(2) With the plan under para. 1, in compliance with the rules and norms of this act, the following may be regulated:
1. existing unregulated land plots, to form a larger number of separate regulated plots;
2. land plots whose size does not meet the requirements of Art. 19, to complete them with parts of neighbouring plots;
3. neighbouring unregulated land plots, to create co-owned regulated plots.

(3) In the cases under para. 2, the owners concerned file an application with the municipality, and in the cases under para. 2, items 2 and 3, also a preliminary contract for the transfer of ownership with notarially certified signatures. The ideal parts of the co-owners in the co-owned regulated plots are set by the contract itself.
(4) When a regulation plan under para. 2, items 2 and 3 affects land plots that are state property, the contract under para. 3 is concluded at market prices by the regional governor in written form.
(5) When a regulation plan under para. 2, items 2 and 3 affects land plots that are municipal property, the contract under para. 3 is concluded at market prices by the mayor in written form.
(6) In the cases under para. 2, items 2 and 3, building may be permitted after the final contract under para. 3, 4 or 5 is presented.

(7) Copies of the effective detailed development plans are sent by the municipality to the Geodesy, Cartography and Cadastre Agency of its own motion. In the cases under para. 2, items 2 and 3, the copies are sent after the final contract under para. 3, 4 or 5 is presented.
Art. 19. (1) When land plots are regulated for low residential building, detached or joined in two plots, the following sizes are kept:
1. in towns: at least 14 m frontage and 300 m² area;
2. in resort settlements and settlement formations and in the resort zones of settlements: at least 16 m frontage and 500 m² area;
3. in villa zones: at least 18 m frontage and 600 m² area;

4. in villages or parts of them on mainly flat ground: at least 16 m frontage and 500 m² area, and in special ground and economic conditions and on main streets, at least 14 m frontage and 300 m² area;
5. in villages or parts of them on mainly steep ground: at least 12 m frontage and 250 m² area.
(2) The villages or parts of them on mainly flat or steep ground are set by a decision of the municipal council on the opinion of the municipal expert council.

(3) The minimum sizes of regulated plots for low building set in para. 1 (frontage and area) may be reduced by at most one fifth, depending on the economic, technical or ground conditions or on the position of existing solid buildings, when this does not worsen the conditions for suitable building, on the opinion of the municipal expert council.
(4) When the land plots under para. 1 are divided, the real parts may not be smaller than the minimum sizes set in para. 1, reduced by at most 1/5.

(5) When land plots are regulated in blocks for medium and high residential building, for low joined building in more than two plots, for social housing or for other specific building, the sizes of the plots are set by the detailed development plan itself, without the norms of para. 1.

(6) When land plots within settlements are regulated for non-residential building or for other needs without building, their sizes are set by the detailed development plan, in line with the sanitary and fire safety requirements and the development rules and norms.

(7) The outlines of streets, squares and regulated plots, their sizes and the building of the plots in settlements or parts of them of historical, archaeological, ethnographic or architectural importance are set by the detailed development plan itself, so as to keep the historical and architectural values, the environment, the typical spatial and architectural image and the valuable trees.

Art. 38. (1) In the above-ground floors of a residential building, besides dwellings, studios and offices for individual creative activity may be built, and on the ground, semi-basement or basement floor, garages or parking places, by exception transformer stations and other objects and facilities of technical infrastructure, in compliance with the sanitary, fire safety and other technical requirements and the safety norms.

(2) Objects for business and service activities in a residential building under construction are placed below the dwellings, if they have separate entrances and meet the sanitary, fire safety and other technical requirements.

(3) In an existing residential building under the condominium regime, an alteration and a change of purpose of a residential room or a separate dwelling into a surgery, an office or a studio for individual creative activity with access of outside persons to the building is allowed if the objects are on the ground or semi-basement floor, the alteration meets the sanitary, fire safety and other technical requirements, and on the express written notarially certified consent of all owners of dwellings who are direct neighbours of the objects. By exception, such objects may also be placed on other above-ground floors only on a decision of the general meeting of the owners of dwellings taken in the prescribed way and with the express written notarially certified consent of all owners of dwellings who are direct neighbours of the object.

(4) An existing residential room or a separate dwelling on the ground floor of a residential building may be altered with a change of purpose into a shop or other service activities, outside those under para. 3, in compliance with the sanitary, fire safety and other technical requirements and if a separate entrance is provided outside the entrance and the common rooms of the residential floors. In these cases a decision of the general meeting of the owners taken in the prescribed way and the express written notarially certified consent of all owners of dwellings who are direct neighbours of the object are required.

(5) Separate objects for non-residential needs built in an existing building may be altered and change their purpose under the general procedure, without the consent of the owners in the condominium, if the requirements of Art. 185(1), items 2–4 are met and no excessive noise or other pollution is caused. If these conditions are not met, the requirements of Art. 185(2) and (3) apply.

(6) The consent of the owners in the condominium is not required to restore the residential purpose of already altered separate rooms and objects for non-residential needs built in an existing residential building.

(7) The designs for alterations under paras. 3–5 must include a reasoned opinion of a structural engineer with full design capacity, proving that the loads do not increase, that structural elements are not affected, and that the bearing capacity, stability and durability of the structure do not decrease; when changes to the structure are needed or the loads increase, a structural part of the design is also presented.

(8) In new buildings under the condominium regime with a building permit issued after the entry into force of the Condominium Management Act, in which more than ten separate objects are planned, at least one common room is provided for the owners and the occupants for household, sports and other service activities, on the ground or the first floor.
(9) An alteration and a change of purpose of objects under paras. 1–5 is not allowed if the necessary garages or parking places for the new objects cannot be provided in the plot.
(10) Exceptions from para. 9 are allowed by the authority that issues the building permit, under the conditions of Art. 43(2).
Art. 147. (1) No approval of investment projects is required for the building permit for:
1. the buildings of the supplementary development, except the buildings for production, public services or trade and the buildings under Art. 151(1);
(The other items of para. 1 and paras. 2–6 are not translated here.)

Art. 177. (1) After the construction is completed and the acceptance tests are finished, when they are needed, the investor files an application with the authority under para. 2 or 3 for putting the object into service, with the final report under Art. 168(6), the contracts with the utility companies for connection to the technical infrastructure networks, a technical passport and an energy performance certificate of a new building, and states the cadastral identifier of the object. For constructions under Art. 32(1), item 1, letters "b" and "g" of the Cadastre and Property Register Act that create zones of restrictions, the investor presents a certificate of the Geodesy, Cartography and Cadastre Agency that they are recorded in the specialised maps and registers. In the cases under Art. 151(1), item 10, the installations are registered with the technical supervision bodies after they are mounted.

(2) Constructions of the first, second and third category are put into service on the basis of a permit for use issued by the bodies of the National Construction Control Directorate, under conditions and procedures set in an ordinance of the Minister of Regional Development and Public Works. The permits for use are published in the Single Public Register of Spatial Development under Art. 5a.

(3) Constructions of the fourth and fifth category are put into service on the basis of a certificate of commissioning from the authority that issued the building permit, under conditions and procedures set in the ordinance under para. 2. The certificate is issued within 7 days from the receipt of the application under para. 1, after a check that the documents are complete and the registration of the commissioning, and the authority may also make an on-site check. The certificates are published in the Single Public Register of Spatial Development under Art. 5a.

(4) The commissioning of constructions and/or facilities of increased danger requires a positive opinion of the technical supervision bodies. For constructions of the first, second and third category, the opinion is given through their participation in the commissions under the ordinance under para. 2. For constructions of the fourth and fifth category, the opinion is given to the authority under para. 3 within 5 days of the request.
(5) The internal installations of the construction are connected to the common networks and facilities of technical infrastructure on the basis of a contract with the utility companies.

(6) For special objects connected with the defence and security of the country, the permit for use is issued by the Minister of Defence, the Minister of Interior, the chairpersons of the State Agency for National Security, the State Intelligence Agency and the State Agency for Technical Operations, or the head of the National Protection Service, respectively.
(7) (Repealed.)
Art. 178. (1) Constructions or parts of them may not be used before the competent authority under Art. 177 has put them into service.
(2) Constructions of the sixth category and the objects under Art. 147a are not put into service.
(3) Constructions are not put into service when:

1. they were not built in line with the approved investment design and the requirements of Art. 169(1) and (3) and Art. 169a(1), and/or no technical passport and no certificate of design energy performance were drawn up;
2. the measures of the part "Vertical planning" were not carried out and the greening under the approved design was not done;
3. existing buildings and structures that are not part of the building scheme and that the design permit provides to be removed were not removed;
4. the façades of the buildings and structures were not finished in line with the approved investment design;

5. the streets, roads or alleys that connect the object with the street or road network and give normal access to the plot were not built, in territories with medium and high building, as well as in resorts, holiday villages, golf villages, aqua parks and other territories for recreation;
6. (Repealed.)
7. no permit or registration document for waste activities was issued, when such is required under Art. 67 and 78 of the Waste Management Act.
(4) Constructions or parts of them may not be used contrary to their purpose or in breach of the conditions of their commissioning.

(5) For breaches of paras. 1 and 4 in constructions of the first to the third category, the head of the National Construction Control Directorate or an official authorised by the head, on the basis of a declaratory act, forbids by a reasoned order the use of the constructions and orders their vacating and the cutting off of their supply of electricity, heat, water, gas, telephone and others. The order binds the suppliers and is carried out at once.
(6) For breaches of paras. 1 and 4 in constructions of the fourth and fifth category, the mayor of the municipality or an official authorised by the mayor does the same under para. 5.

(7) For breaches of paras. 1 and 4 in special objects connected with defence and security, the competent minister or chairperson under Art. 177(6) forbids by a reasoned order the occupation or use of the constructions and orders the actions needed to bring them in line with the permit for use and the other building documents.
(8) After the causes of the ban are removed and the fines and fees due are paid, the commissioning is permitted or certified by the authorities under Art. 177.
(9) The streets, roads or alleys under para. 3, item 5 may also be built at the owners' expense under the conditions and procedure of the ordinance under Art. 69(2).
Art. 181. (1) The right to build a building or a part of it may be the object of a transfer from the moment it is created until the building is completed in rough construction.
(2) After the building is completed in rough construction, the object of a transfer may be the built building or separate parts of it.

(3) The completion of the building in rough construction is stated by a protocol under the ordinance under Art. 168(3), drawn up by the person exercising construction supervision in the presence of the investor, the builder, the designer and an official under Art. 223(2).
Art. 183. (1) In a co-owned regulated land plot, a new building, adding floors or an extension may be built by one or more co-owners on the basis of a contract in notarial form with the other owners.

(2) Adding floors or an extension to a building under the condominium regime is permitted on the basis of a contract creating a right to add floors or an extension with the owner of the regulated land plot in notarial form, and a declaration of consent with notarially certified signatures of all owners in the condominium.

(3) When the state or the municipality is a co-owner of a regulated land plot, the contracts under paras. 1 and 2 are concluded in written form. When the state or the municipality owns a property in a building under the condominium regime, the consent under para. 2 is in written form. The conditions and procedure for these contracts and for the consent are set by the implementing regulations of the State Property Act and by the ordinance under Art. 8(2) of the Municipal Property Act respectively.

(4) For a permit for a new building, adding floors or an extension in a co-owned property intended for low residential or villa building, the consent of the other co-owners is not required when they have built, started or hold rights to the respective building in the property.
Art. 185. (1) The consent of the other owners in the condominium is not required for alterations of one's own objects, rooms or parts of them when:
1. their purpose does not change;
2. common rooms and areas or parts of them are not taken and their purpose does not change;
3. the common parts of the building are not changed substantially;
4. internal installations are connected with common networks that pass through or next to the partition wall or through service rooms on one vertical axis;
5. a new installation is laid through a common part without affecting the rooms of individual owners;
6. the purpose of objects in non-residential buildings changes;
7. the alteration is made under the conditions of Art. 38(5) and (6).

(2) Outside the cases under para. 1, a decision of the general meeting of the owners taken in the prescribed way and the express written consent of all owners who are direct neighbours of the object are required, and when common parts are taken, the consent of all owners expressed with notarially certified signatures.

(3) When the design for an alteration provides for joining a common part of a condominium building to a separate object in the condominium, or for creating a separate object from a common part of the building, a contract for the transfer of ownership in notarial form is concluded with the other owners in the condominium. The building permit is issued on the basis of the approved design and the contract.

(4) The state and the municipalities conclude the contracts under para. 3 under the conditions and procedure set by the implementing regulations of the State Property Act and by the ordinance under Art. 8(2) of the Municipal Property Act respectively.

(5) The alteration under paras. 1 and 2 is allowed only if no other technical solution can be found, it meets the architectural, structural, sanitary and fire safety rules and norms, and it is made in the way most favourable for the property affected.
(6) In the cases under paras. 1 and 2, the owner of the altered rooms must repair all damage caused by the construction works, and Art. 210 applies.
(7) The alteration under para. 3 is noted in the cadastre, and the contracts under paras. 3 and 4 are entered in the property register.

Art. 190. (1) When under a detailed development plan some regulated land plots have frontage only on new streets that are designed but not yet opened, the municipality may lay temporary roads that give access to these plots.

(2) When needed, temporary roads are laid in regulated parts of settlements and settlement formations for which new detailed development plans will be made, and in unregulated parts included in a general development plan.

(3) Temporary roads should follow, as far as possible, the new streets under the detailed development plan, the draft plan or the studies made. They are laid so as not to affect existing buildings and structures and long-lived decorative trees.
(4) The ownership of the parts of land plots used for temporary roads is kept. Temporary roads are used until the new streets under the detailed development plan are opened.

(5) When there is no other technical possibility, temporary roads are also laid to give access to lawfully permitted constructions outside the urbanised territories, until the use of the constructions is permitted, together with their permanent roads.

(6) Temporary roads are laid on the basis of a written contract between the owners of the land plots concerned with notarially certified signatures, and without agreement, on the basis of an order of the mayor of the municipality.
(7) Temporary roads in disasters, accidents and catastrophes are laid on the basis of an order of the competent bodies set by a special law.
Art. 192. (1) A right of passage through another person's land plot is created by a written contract with notarially certified signatures.

(2) When the owners of the land plots do not agree and another technical solution is clearly not economically reasonable, the right of passage through other land plots is created by an order of the mayor of the municipality.

(3) A right of passage through state or municipal land plots is created, when another technical solution is clearly not economically reasonable, by an order of the regional governor or of the mayor of the municipality respectively.

(4) The right of passage may not worsen the conditions for building on the land plots, prevent the established way of permanent use of the plots or affect permitted constructions or existing buildings, unless the owners expressly agree on it in the contract under para. 1.

(5) A worsening of the conditions for building and use of state or municipal land plots when a right of passage to other properties is created may be allowed by exception, for lack of another technical possibility or when another technical solution is clearly not economically reasonable, with the permission of the Minister of Regional Development and Public Works for state plots, or by a decision of the municipal council for municipal plots.
(6) The price of the right of passage under paras. 2 and 3 is set under Art. 210 and is paid before the orders under paras. 2 and 3 are issued.

(7) The contract under para. 1 and the order under para. 2 are entered in the property register in the partida of the land plot served by the right of passage and in the partida of the land plot on which the right of passage is created.

(8) The order under para. 3 is entered in the property register in the partida of the land plot served by the right of passage, in the partida of the state or municipal land plot on which the right is created, and in the act of state or municipal property.

Art. 193. (1) The right to lay branches of common networks and facilities of technical infrastructure through other properties is created by a written contract between the owners of the land plots with notarially certified signatures.
(2) By the contract under para. 1, the right is acquired to build the branch of the common technical infrastructure network in the other property and to acquire its ownership.
(3) When the owners do not agree and another technical solution is clearly not economically reasonable, the right is created by an order of the mayor of the municipality.

(4) The right to lay branches of common networks and facilities of technical infrastructure through state or municipal land plots is created, when another technical solution is clearly not economically reasonable, by an order of the regional governor or of the mayor of the municipality respectively.

(5) Laying such branches may not worsen the conditions for building on the land plots, prevent the established way of permanent use of the plots or affect permitted constructions or existing buildings, unless the owners expressly agree on it in the contract under para. 1.

(6) A worsening of the conditions for building and use of state or municipal land plots because of such branches to other properties may be allowed by exception, for lack of another technical possibility or when another technical solution is clearly not economically reasonable, with the permission of the Minister of Regional Development and Public Works for state plots, or by a decision of the municipal council for municipal plots.
(7) The building permit for the branches is issued to the holder of the right created under paras. 1, 3 and 4.
(8) The price of the right created under paras. 3 and 4 is set under Art. 210 and is paid before the orders under paras. 3 and 4 are issued.

(9) The contract under para. 1 and the order under para. 3 are entered in the property register in the partida of the land plot served by the right to lay the branches and in the partida of the land plot through which the branches are laid.

(10) The order under para. 4 is entered in the property register in the partida of the land plot served by the right, in the partida of the state or municipal land plot through which the branches are laid, and in the act of state or municipal property.

(11) In disasters, accidents and catastrophes, branches of common networks to individual objects may be laid temporarily, until the consequences are overcome, through other properties on the basis of an order of the competent bodies set by a special law. In that case no building permit is issued.

(12) For the damage under para. 11, the owners of the properties affected are compensated directly after the disaster, accident or catastrophe is brought under control, under the conditions and procedure of a special law.

Art. 200. (1) Real parts of land plots within the boundaries of settlements and settlement formations may be acquired by legal transactions or by prescription only if the minimum sizes under Art. 19 are met.

(2) The rule of para. 1 does not apply when the part of the land plot joins a neighbouring plot under the conditions of Art. 17 and the remaining part meets the requirements of Art. 19 or joins a neighbouring plot.
(3) (Repealed.)
Art. 201. (1) In a court partition of a regulated land plot to form new regulated plots, the court asks the municipal (district) administration for an opinion on whether the property can be divided.

(2) Regulated land plots cannot be divided when no design can be made to divide them into two or more parts without creating a position of existing buildings or permitted constructions that the law does not allow, and without creating regulated plots with a frontage and an area below the minimum that the law sets for the character and manner of building in the building plan of the divided property.

(3) When the regulated plot can be divided, the chief architect of the municipality (district), by a reasoned instruction to the parties, orders them to submit a draft change of the regulation plan in force. The order changing the regulation plan enters into force under Art. 15(6) and applies after the court decision on the partition becomes final.
(4) When the regulated plot cannot be divided, the chief architect sends an opinion to the court within 14 days from the receipt of the court's request under para. 1.

(5) The court considers the opinion of the chief architect under para. 4. When it finds the opinion unfounded and the obstacles under para. 2 absent, the court gives binding instructions by a ruling to change the regulation plan under para. 3.

Art. 202. A voluntary partition of a co-owned building, dwelling or other object, and legal transactions transferring real parts of them, may be made only if the separated shares or parts match investment designs approved for this, except for the objects under Art. 147(1), item 1. This is certified by the municipal (district) administration.
§ 5. In the meaning of this Act:
2. "Land plot" is a part of the territory, including a part permanently covered with water, with boundaries set according to the right of ownership.

11. "Regulated land plot" or "regulated plot" is a land plot for which a detailed development plan set the boundaries, the access from a street, road or alley, the specific purpose and the development rules.
46. "Rough construction" is a building or structure whose outer walls and roof are finished, with or without finishing works.
(The other items of § 5 are not translated here.)
